intro: Picture this: you wake up, open the door of your curved-wall Hobbit-style room, step onto the balcony to find a sea of mist floating across the valley, then drive just one minute to Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew — Kiri Pura Resort (Kiripura Resort) is a small boutique resort on Khao Kho, in Khaem Son, Phetchabun, that plays with a "Hobbit room" concept, and the thing people talk about most is that many rooms have an in-room steam room · it offers mookata service on site, breakfast with mountain views, and sits within walking distance of a strawberry farm and viewpoints · from about THB 2,000/night, rated 9.3 from real reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: Who Kiri Pura Resort is for — the shortest way to put it: Kiripura Resort is for people who want to head up Khao Kho to quietly "recharge" in somewhere with real character, not the same cookie-cutter chain hotel room over and over · its calling card is the "Hobbit" style rooms with rounded walls and woodwork that look warm and photograph well, plus details that are hard to find at this price like an in-room steam room, which has become a highlight many reviews mention · this is a small boutique resort with only a handful of rooms, so the feel is fairly private and unhurried · real reviews line up on who fits best here: couples after a romantic stay with photo corners, small families who want to stay near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew without long drives, and groups of friends who want to set up a mookata spread in the resort in the cool air · another group that says they loved it is people who come to Khao Kho to chase the morning sea of mist, because the resort sits on high ground in the Khaem Son zone where early mornings often bring mist floating across the valley · on the flip side, if you expect a big resort with a pool, gym, and every facility like a 5-star hotel, this may not be the answer, because Kiri Pura's charm is in being a small boutique with character rather than a full set of facilities.

Location and getting there — this is Kiri Pura's clearest strength · the resort sits in Khaem Son, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun, and is only about 0.6 kilometers from Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew, roughly a 1-minute drive, which is very close compared with many Khao Kho stays that require driving up and down the mountain for tens of minutes to reach each sight · nearby points of interest are close too, like the strawberry farm (Doi Pah Gaew) around 1 kilometer away and viewpoints/sky walk in the same zone, making it easy to plan days without long drives · as for getting here, Khao Kho has no airport of its own; the nearest and most-used one is Phitsanulok Airport (PHS), which is a fair distance away (over a hundred kilometers once you add the mountain route), so most people drive their own car or rent one, since touring Khao Kho really depends on having a car · an important thing to know is that the road up Khao Kho has steep grades and plenty of curves, so check your car and brakes, especially if driving in the evening or in the rainy season when mist can roll in heavily · once you arrive there is free parking on site, so you can use your car as a base for exploring around Khao Kho.

"We chose this place because it's right by Wat Pha Sorn Kaew. In the morning it's a quick drive and you're there, no wasting time driving up and down the mountain. The rooms are so cute, with curved walls like a house out of a movie, and the air is lovely and cool. Early mornings there's even mist floating around for photos."

Room types and decor — Kiri Pura is a boutique resort with several room styles to choose from based on group size and budget · the signature is the curved-wall Hobbit-style room at around 21 sqm, designed to feel warm with woodwork and natural tones, with a view balcony, and the part people talk about is that it has an in-room steam room, a detail rarely found at this level · stepping up there is the loft-style Standard Balcony at around 44 sqm, roomier and good for couples or groups of friends · the top room, the Superior Jacuzzi at around 45 sqm, comes with a jacuzzi you can soak in while looking at the mountains, with fancier decor and the option of an extra bed for families or groups · there are also Deluxe and Family rooms and tent/camping options for those who want to feel closer to nature · overall, reviews agree the rooms are cute, full of character, photograph well, are clean, and have spacious, easy-to-use bathrooms · every room leans into the views and cool air of Khao Kho, and some open onto a full mountain view from the balcony, which is worth asking about when booking if the view matters to you · one observation found in reviews is that some fittings, like power outlets or the TV remote, may glitch in some rooms, which you can flag to the team to sort out.

Facilities and what makes it relaxing — being a small boutique resort, Kiri Pura doesn't go for big-resort facilities but picks features that "match a Khao Kho trip" · the most-talked-about highlight is the in-room steam room that helps you unwind on cool evenings, and the mountain-view jacuzzi in the Superior Jacuzzi room that suits couples really well · the common areas have a garden, lounging corners, and a picnic spot to sit in the cool breeze and take photos, plus a sauna, bar, and karaoke for groups who want some light socializing at the resort · there is Wi-Fi and free parking, as well as room service · to be straight about it, there is no swimming pool and no gym, because the concept is relaxing close to nature on the mountain, not a sporty resort or pool villa · if the point of your trip is to breathe the cool air, chase the sea of mist, visit temples and viewpoints, then come back to sleep comfortably in a room with character, this set of facilities is a good fit for actual use · note that some reviews mention the sauna or hot-water system not working fully at certain times, so it's worth checking the latest status with the resort first if you specifically plan to use that part.

Food and in-house mookata — dining is another thing that sets Kiri Pura apart from typical Khao Kho stays · the highlight is mookata service at the resort (starting in the several-hundred-baht range per set) that lets guests set up a spread in the cool, comfortable air without driving out to find a restaurant in the evening, a charm that suits a Khao Kho trip with friends or family very well · as for breakfast, many reviews praise the view — you sit and eat while looking at the mountains and the morning sea of mist, a moment many say is worth the early start · the food overall is decent in the style of fresh-cooked Thai food at a small resort · to be fair, some voices in reviews say the breakfast menu options are fairly limited, not a big varied buffet like a chain hotel, which is normal for a small boutique stay · the upside is that Khao Kho has plenty of restaurants and cafes with lovely views spread around, so heading out to find other meals is part of the fun of the trip anyway.

Service — service is a point that earns fairly steady praise in real reviews · being a small resort, the care leans warm and friendly, like owner-run hospitality rather than the scripted service of a big hotel · many guests mention an attentive team that helps recommend sights, routes, and the best times to see the sea of mist, and handles the mookata and breakfast well · one thing to understand is that a small mountain stay like this naturally has fewer staff than a city hotel, so on long-weekend peaks when it's full, some responses may be slower than usual, which is understandable and doesn't dent the overall impression · on the whole, service is a strength that adds to the boutique charm here.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — gathered from Trip.com, Agoda, and Thai travel-review sources like Chillpainai, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: a location very close to Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, just a minute's drive; cute Hobbit-style rooms with character that photograph well; the in-room steam room as an above-expectations touch; lovely cool air with a chance of the sea of mist in the early morning; clean rooms and spacious bathrooms; friendly service; and in-house mookata that is fun for groups of friends and families · on the watch-out side: what comes up is some fittings in certain rooms, like a broken outlet in the bathroom or a dead TV remote battery, or hot water arriving slowly / weakly at times, with reports that the sauna is out of service in some periods · on top of that, the breakfast options are fairly limited and there is no swimming pool · most of these gripes are typical of a small boutique stay that can be fixed by flagging the team and setting the right expectations, rather than big problems that put people off returning · overall, the 9.3 score from reviews on Trip.com reflects that most experiences come out positive.

"The in-room steam room was such a surprise. After the steam, a hot shower, then sitting out on the balcony in the cool breeze — so blissful. The one small gripe is the hot water comes a bit slow in the morning, but I told the staff and they took good care of it. Coming back to stay again next time."

Price and value — Kiri Pura's room rates start at about THB 2,000/night for entry-level rooms in the regular season, rising with room type and timing, with bigger rooms like the Superior Jacuzzi or the winter high season climbing into the several-thousand-baht-per-night range · compared with other Khao Kho stays, Kiri Pura feels good value in terms of character and location rather than competing on the number of facilities — what you pay for is a room with its own design, an in-room steam room, and a spot that's a one-minute drive to Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, which genuinely saves driving up and down the mountain each day · for couples who want a romantic room that photographs well, or groups who want to set up a mookata spread at the resort in the cool air, this price is reasonable · but if you compare it with a big resort that has a pool and a varied breakfast buffet, understand that Kiri Pura plays a different game — emphasizing atmosphere and privacy over a full range of services · the tip is to compare prices across several platforms and book ahead in winter, because the good stays on Khao Kho fill up fast and prices climb quickly.

Things to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, if you want a steam room or jacuzzi, specify the room type clearly when booking, because not every room has this feature · two, if you're set on seeing the sea of mist, your best chance is late rainy season to early winter (October–February), and you should wake up early because the mist usually comes at dawn · three, ask about hot water and the sauna's status in advance if these features are the main reason you chose to stay · four, if you want mookata at the resort, give advance notice so the team can prepare the ingredients · five, the road up Khao Kho is steep and winding, so prepare your car and brakes, and drive slowly, especially in the evening or in mist · six, in winter and on long weekends rooms fill up fast, so book ahead and pick a free-cancellation option for now if your plans aren't set.

Summary — from all the real reviews, Kiri Pura Resort is the best fit for people who want to stay on Khao Kho somewhere with character, near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, with a private feel · the Hobbit-style rooms, in-room steam room, mountain-view jacuzzi, in-house mookata, and a location that's a one-minute drive to Wat Pha Sorn Kaew give it a charm that's hard to find at this price · if you're after a big resort with a pool, gym, and a varied breakfast buffet, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a larger resort on Khao Kho instead · but for a Khao Kho trip where you want a cute stay that photographs well, cool air, and the closest spot to the main sights — Kiri Pura matches that need well in its own boutique-mountain way, and that's why it earns such high review scores.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Kiri Pura Resort Khao Kho

faq.q: Where is Kiri Pura Resort, and how close is it to Wat Pha Sorn Kaew?
faq.a: The resort is in Khaem Son, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun Province · it's only about 0.6 kilometers from Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew, roughly a 1-minute drive · it's near a strawberry farm and viewpoints in the same zone, so you can tour Khao Kho without long drives up and down the mountain.

faq.q: Do Kiri Pura's rooms really have an in-room steam room?
faq.a: Yes · the resort's signature is Hobbit-style rooms where many have an in-room steam room, and the Superior Jacuzzi room also has a mountain-view jacuzzi · but not every room has this feature, so specify the room type clearly when booking, and ask about the latest hot water/sauna status first if that's your main reason for staying.

faq.q: What does Kiri Pura Resort start at, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 2,000/night for entry-level rooms in the regular season · there are Standard Hobbit-style rooms, loft-style Standard Balcony rooms, the Superior Jacuzzi with a mountain-view soaking tub, and a Family Room · prices climb quickly in winter and on long weekends, so book ahead and compare across several platforms.

faq.q: Who is Kiri Pura Resort for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples who want a romantic room that photographs well, small families, and groups of friends who want to set up a mookata spread at the stay in the cool air on Khao Kho · it suits people who want to stay near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew and chase the morning sea of mist · if you want a big resort with a pool and gym, a larger Khao Kho property may suit you better.

faq.q: Does Kiri Pura have mookata and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes · it has mookata service at the resort so you can set up a spread in the cool air without heading out (give advance notice) · and there's breakfast with mountain views that many reviews praise for the atmosphere, though the menu options are fairly limited given the boutique size.

faq.q: How do you get to Kiri Pura Resort, and what's the mountain road like?
faq.a: Khao Kho has no airport of its own; the nearest is Phitsanulok Airport (PHS), so most people drive their own car or rent one, since touring Khao Kho depends on having a car · the road up Khao Kho is steep and winding, so check your brakes and drive slowly, especially in the evening or in the rainy season when mist rolls in heavily · the resort has free parking.
